paragraphs.text: Now a certain man was sick, Lazarus of Bethany, of the village of Mary and her sister Martha.
paragraphs.original: Ἦν δέ τις ἀσθενῶν, Λάζαρος ἀπὸ Βηθανίας ἐκ τῆς κώμης Μαρίας καὶ Μάρθας τῆς ἀδελφῆς αὐτῆς.
paragraphs.translit: Ēn de tis asthenōn, Lazaros apo Bēthanias ek tēs kōmēs Marias kai Marthas tēs adelphēs autēs.

paragraphs.text: And it was that Mary who anointed the Lord with ointment, and wiped his feet with her hair, whose brother Lazarus was sick.
paragraphs.original: ἦν δὲ Μαριὰμ ἡ ἀλείψασα τὸν κύριον μύρῳ καὶ ἐκμάξασα τοὺς πόδας αὐτοῦ ταῖς θριξὶν αὐτῆς, ἧς ὁ ἀδελφὸς Λάζαρος ἠσθένει.
paragraphs.translit: ēn de Mariam hē aleipsasa ton kyrion myrō kai ekmaxasa tous podas autou tais thrixin autēs, hēs ho adelphos Lazaros ēsthenei.

paragraphs.text: The sisters therefore sent unto him, saying, Lord, behold, he whom thou lovest is sick.
paragraphs.original: ἀπέστειλαν οὖν αἱ ἀδελφαὶ πρὸς αὐτὸν λέγουσαι· Κύριε, ἴδε ὃν φιλεῖς ἀσθενεῖ.
paragraphs.translit: apesteilan oun hai adelphai pros auton legousai· Kyrie, ide hon phileis asthenei.

paragraphs.text: But when Jesus heard it, he said, This sickness is not unto death, but for the glory of God, that the Son of God may be glorified thereby.
paragraphs.original: ἀκούσας δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν· Αὕτη ἡ ἀσθένεια οὐκ ἔστιν πρὸς θάνατον ἀλλʼ ὑπὲρ τῆς δόξης τοῦ θεοῦ ἵνα δοξασθῇ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ θεοῦ διʼ αὐτῆς.
paragraphs.translit: akousas de ho Iēsous eipen· Hautē hē astheneia ouk estin pros thanaton allʼ hyper tēs doxēs tou theou hina doxasthē ho hyios tou theou diʼ autēs.

paragraphs.text: Now Jesus loved Martha, and her sister, and Lazarus.
paragraphs.original: ἠγάπα δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς τὴν Μάρθαν καὶ τὴν ἀδελφὴν αὐτῆς καὶ τὸν Λάζαρον.
paragraphs.translit: ēgapa de ho Iēsous tēn Marthan kai tēn adelphēn autēs kai ton Lazaron.

paragraphs.text: When therefore he heard that he was sick, he abode at that time two days in the place where he was.
paragraphs.original: ὡς οὖν ἤκουσεν ὅτι ἀσθενεῖ, τότε μὲν ἔμεινεν ἐν ᾧ ἦν τόπῳ δύο ἡμέρας·
paragraphs.translit: hōs oun ēkousen hoti asthenei, tote men emeinen en hō ēn topō dyo hēmeras·

paragraphs.text: Then after this he saith to the disciples, Let us go into Judaea again.
paragraphs.original: ἔπειτα μετὰ τοῦτο λέγει τοῖς μαθηταῖς· Ἄγωμεν εἰς τὴν Ἰουδαίαν πάλιν.
paragraphs.translit: epeita meta touto legei tois mathētais· Agōmen eis tēn Ioudaian palin.

paragraphs.text: The disciples say unto him, Rabbi, the Jews were but now seeking to stone thee; and goest thou thither again?
paragraphs.original: λέγουσιν αὐτῷ οἱ μαθηταί· Ῥαββί, νῦν ἐζήτουν σε λιθάσαι οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι, καὶ πάλιν ὑπάγεις ἐκεῖ;
paragraphs.translit: legousin autō hoi mathētai· Rhabbi, nyn ezētoun se lithasai hoi Ioudaioi, kai palin hypageis ekei;

paragraphs.text: Jesus answered, Are there not twelve hours in the day? If a man walk in the day, he stumbleth not, because he seeth the light of this world.
paragraphs.original: ἀπεκρίθη Ἰησοῦς· Οὐχὶ δώδεκα ὧραί εἰσιν τῆς ἡμέρας; ἐάν τις περιπατῇ ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ, οὐ προσκόπτει, ὅτι τὸ φῶς τοῦ κόσμου τούτου βλέπει·
paragraphs.translit: apekrithē Iēsous· Ouchi dōdeka hōrai eisin tēs hēmeras; ean tis peripatē en tē hēmera, ou proskoptei, hoti to phōs tou kosmou toutou blepei·

paragraphs.text: But if a man walk in the night, he stumbleth, because the light is not in him.
paragraphs.original: ἐὰν δέ τις περιπατῇ ἐν τῇ νυκτί, προσκόπτει, ὅτι τὸ φῶς οὐκ ἔστιν ἐν αὐτῷ.
paragraphs.translit: ean de tis peripatē en tē nykti, proskoptei, hoti to phōs ouk estin en autō.

paragraphs.text: These things spake he: and after this he saith unto them, Our friend Lazarus is fallen asleep; but I go, that I may awake him out of sleep.
paragraphs.original: ταῦτα εἶπεν, καὶ μετὰ τοῦτο λέγει αὐτοῖς· Λάζαρος ὁ φίλος ἡμῶν κεκοίμηται, ἀλλὰ πορεύομαι ἵνα ἐξυπνίσω αὐτόν.
paragraphs.translit: tauta eipen, kai meta touto legei autois· Lazaros ho philos hēmōn kekoimētai, alla poreuomai hina exypnisō auton.

paragraphs.text: The disciples therefore said unto him, Lord, if he is fallen asleep, he will recover.
paragraphs.original: εἶπαν οὖν οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτῷ· Κύριε, εἰ κεκοίμηται σωθήσεται.
paragraphs.translit: eipan oun hoi mathētai autō· Kyrie, ei kekoimētai sōthēsetai.

paragraphs.text: Now Jesus had spoken of his death: but they thought that he spake of taking rest in sleep.
paragraphs.original: εἰρήκει δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς περὶ τοῦ θανάτου αὐτοῦ. ἐκεῖνοι δὲ ἔδοξαν ὅτι περὶ τῆς κοιμήσεως τοῦ ὕπνου λέγει.
paragraphs.translit: eirēkei de ho Iēsous peri tou thanatou autou. ekeinoi de edoxan hoti peri tēs koimēseōs tou hypnou legei.

paragraphs.text: Then Jesus therefore said unto them plainly, Lazarus is dead.
paragraphs.original: τότε οὖν εἶπεν αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς παρρησίᾳ· Λάζαρος ἀπέθανεν,
paragraphs.translit: tote oun eipen autois ho Iēsous parrēsia· Lazaros apethanen,

paragraphs.text: And I am glad for your sakes that I was not there, to the intent ye may believe; nevertheless let us go unto him.
paragraphs.original: καὶ χαίρω διʼ ὑμᾶς, ἵνα πιστεύσητε, ὅτι οὐκ ἤμην ἐκεῖ· ἀλλὰ ἄγωμεν πρὸς αὐτόν.
paragraphs.translit: kai chairō diʼ hymas, hina pisteusēte, hoti ouk ēmēn ekei· alla agōmen pros auton.

paragraphs.text: Thomas therefore, who is called Didymus, said unto his fellow-disciples, Let us also go, that we may die with him.
paragraphs.original: εἶπεν οὖν Θωμᾶς ὁ λεγόμενος Δίδυμος τοῖς συμμαθηταῖς· Ἄγωμεν καὶ ἡμεῖς ἵνα ἀποθάνωμεν μετʼ αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: eipen oun Thōmas ho legomenos Didymos tois symmathētais· Agōmen kai hēmeis hina apothanōmen metʼ autou.

paragraphs.text: So when Jesus came, he found that he had been in the tomb four days already.
paragraphs.original: Ἐλθὼν οὖν ὁ Ἰησοῦς εὗρεν αὐτὸν τέσσαρας ἤδη ἡμέρας ἔχοντα ἐν τῷ μνημείῳ.
paragraphs.translit: Elthōn oun ho Iēsous heuren auton tessaras ēdē hēmeras echonta en tō mnēmeiō.

paragraphs.text: Now Bethany was nigh unto Jerusalem, about fifteen furlongs off;
paragraphs.original: ἦν δὲ ἡ Βηθανία ἐγγὺς τῶν Ἱεροσολύμων ὡς ἀπὸ σταδίων δεκαπέντε.
paragraphs.translit: ēn de hē Bēthania engys tōn Hierosolymōn hōs apo stadiōn dekapente.

paragraphs.text: and many of the Jews had come to Martha and Mary, to console them concerning their brother.
paragraphs.original: πολλοὶ δὲ ἐκ τῶν Ἰουδαίων ἐληλύθεισαν πρὸς τὴν Μάρθαν καὶ Μαριὰμ ἵνα παραμυθήσωνται αὐτὰς περὶ τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: polloi de ek tōn Ioudaiōn elēlytheisan pros tēn Marthan kai Mariam hina paramythēsōntai autas peri tou adelphou.

paragraphs.text: Martha therefore, when she heard that Jesus was coming, went and met him: but Mary still sat in the house.
paragraphs.original: ἡ οὖν Μάρθα ὡς ἤκουσεν ὅτι Ἰησοῦς ἔρχεται ὑπήντησεν αὐτῷ· Μαρία δὲ ἐν τῷ οἴκῳ ἐκαθέζετο.
paragraphs.translit: hē oun Martha hōs ēkousen hoti Iēsous erchetai hypēntēsen autō· Maria de en tō oikō ekathezeto.

paragraphs.text: Martha therefore said unto Jesus, Lord, if thou hadst been here, my brother had not died.
paragraphs.original: εἶπεν οὖν ἡ Μάρθα πρὸς τὸν Ἰησοῦν· Κύριε, εἰ ἦς ὧδε οὐκ ἂν ἀπέθανεν ὁ ἀδελφός μου·
paragraphs.translit: eipen oun hē Martha pros ton Iēsoun· Kyrie, ei ēs hōde ouk an apethanen ho adelphos mou·

paragraphs.text: And even now I know that, whatsoever thou shalt ask of God, God will give thee.
paragraphs.original: καὶ νῦν οἶδα ὅτι ὅσα ἂν αἰτήσῃ τὸν θεὸν δώσει σοι ὁ θεός.
paragraphs.translit: kai nyn oida hoti hosa an aitēsē ton theon dōsei soi ho theos.

paragraphs.text: Jesus saith unto her, Thy brother shall rise again.
paragraphs.original: λέγει αὐτῇ ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Ἀναστήσεται ὁ ἀδελφός σου.
paragraphs.translit: legei autē ho Iēsous· Anastēsetai ho adelphos sou.

paragraphs.text: Martha saith unto him, I know that he shall rise again in the resurrection at the last day.
paragraphs.original: λέγει αὐτῷ ἡ Μάρθα· Οἶδα ὅτι ἀναστήσεται ἐν τῇ ἀναστάσει ἐν τῇ ἐσχάτῃ ἡμέρᾳ.
paragraphs.translit: legei autō hē Martha· Oida hoti anastēsetai en tē anastasei en tē eschatē hēmera.

paragraphs.text: Jesus said unto her, I am the resurrection, and the life: he that believeth on me, though he die, yet shall he live;
paragraphs.original: εἶπεν αὐτῇ ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Ἐγώ εἰμι ἡ ἀνάστασις καὶ ἡ ζωή· ὁ πιστεύων εἰς ἐμὲ κἂν ἀποθάνῃ ζήσεται,
paragraphs.translit: eipen autē ho Iēsous· Egō eimi hē anastasis kai hē zōē· ho pisteuōn eis eme kan apothanē zēsetai,

paragraphs.text: and whosoever liveth and believeth on me shall never die. Believest thou this?
paragraphs.original: καὶ πᾶς ὁ ζῶν καὶ πιστεύων εἰς ἐμὲ οὐ μὴ ἀποθάνῃ εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα· πιστεύεις τοῦτο;
paragraphs.translit: kai pas ho zōn kai pisteuōn eis eme ou mē apothanē eis ton aiōna· pisteueis touto;

paragraphs.text: She saith unto him, Yea, Lord: I have believed that thou art the Christ, the Son of God, [even] he that cometh into the world.
paragraphs.original: λέγει αὐτῷ· Ναί, κύριε· ἐγὼ πεπίστευκα ὅτι σὺ εἶ ὁ χριστὸς ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ θεοῦ ὁ εἰς τὸν κόσμον ἐρχόμενος.
paragraphs.translit: legei autō· Nai, kyrie· egō pepisteuka hoti sy ei ho christos ho hyios tou theou ho eis ton kosmon erchomenos.

paragraphs.text: And when she had said this, she went away, and called Mary her sister secretly, saying, The Teacher is her, and calleth thee.
paragraphs.original: Καὶ τοῦτο εἰποῦσα ἀπῆλθεν καὶ ἐφώνησεν Μαριὰμ τὴν ἀδελφὴν αὐτῆς λάθρᾳ εἰποῦσα· Ὁ διδάσκαλος πάρεστιν καὶ φωνεῖ σε.
paragraphs.translit: Kai touto eipousa apēlthen kai ephōnēsen Mariam tēn adelphēn autēs lathra eipousa· Ho didaskalos parestin kai phōnei se.

paragraphs.text: And she, when she heard it, arose quickly, and went unto him.
paragraphs.original: ἐκείνη δὲ ὡς ἤκουσεν ἠγέρθη ταχὺ καὶ ἤρχετο πρὸς αὐτόν·
paragraphs.translit: ekeinē de hōs ēkousen ēgerthē tachy kai ērcheto pros auton·

paragraphs.text: (Now Jesus was not yet come into the village, but was still in the place where Martha met him.)
paragraphs.original: οὔπω δὲ ἐληλύθει ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἰς τὴν κώμην, ἀλλʼ ἦν ἔτι ἐν τῷ τόπῳ ὅπου ὑπήντησεν αὐτῷ ἡ Μάρθα.
paragraphs.translit: oupō de elēlythei ho Iēsous eis tēn kōmēn, allʼ ēn eti en tō topō hopou hypēntēsen autō hē Martha.

paragraphs.text: The Jews then who were with her in the house, and were consoling her, when they saw Mary, that she rose up quickly and went out, followed her, supposing that she was going unto the tomb to weep there.
paragraphs.original: οἱ οὖν Ἰουδαῖοι οἱ ὄντες μετʼ αὐτῆς ἐν τῇ οἰκίᾳ καὶ παραμυθούμενοι αὐτήν, ἰδόντες τὴν Μαριὰμ ὅτι ταχέως ἀνέστη καὶ ἐξῆλθεν, ἠκολούθησαν αὐτῇ δόξαντες ὅτι ὑπάγει εἰς τὸ μνημεῖον ἵνα κλαύσῃ ἐκεῖ.
paragraphs.translit: hoi oun Ioudaioi hoi ontes metʼ autēs en tē oikia kai paramythoumenoi autēn, idontes tēn Mariam hoti tacheōs anestē kai exēlthen, ēkolouthēsan autē doxantes hoti hypagei eis to mnēmeion hina klausē ekei.

paragraphs.text: Mary therefore, when she came where Jesus was, and saw him, fell down at his feet, saying unto him, Lord, if thou hadst been here, my brother had not died.
paragraphs.original: ἡ οὖν Μαριὰμ ὡς ἦλθεν ὅπου ἦν Ἰησοῦς ἰδοῦσα αὐτὸν ἔπεσεν αὐτοῦ πρὸς τοὺς πόδας, λέγουσα αὐτῷ· Κύριε, εἰ ἦς ὧδε οὐκ ἄν μου ἀπέθανεν ὁ ἀδελφός.
paragraphs.translit: hē oun Mariam hōs ēlthen hopou ēn Iēsous idousa auton epesen autou pros tous podas, legousa autō· Kyrie, ei ēs hōde ouk an mou apethanen ho adelphos.

paragraphs.text: When Jesus therefore saw her weeping, and the Jews [also] weeping who came with her, he groaned in the spirit, and was troubled,
paragraphs.original: Ἰησοῦς οὖν ὡς εἶδεν αὐτὴν κλαίουσαν καὶ τοὺς συνελθόντας αὐτῇ Ἰουδαίους κλαίοντας ἐνεβριμήσατο τῷ πνεύματι καὶ ἐτάραξεν ἑαυτόν,
paragraphs.translit: Iēsous oun hōs eiden autēn klaiousan kai tous synelthontas autē Ioudaious klaiontas enebrimēsato tō pneumati kai etaraxen heauton,

paragraphs.text: and said, Where have ye laid him? They say unto him, Lord, come and see.
paragraphs.original: καὶ εἶπεν· Ποῦ τεθείκατε αὐτόν; λέγουσιν αὐτῷ· Κύριε, ἔρχου καὶ ἴδε.
paragraphs.translit: kai eipen· Pou tetheikate auton; legousin autō· Kyrie, erchou kai ide.

paragraphs.text: Jesus wept.
paragraphs.original: ἐδάκρυσεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς.
paragraphs.translit: edakrysen ho Iēsous.

paragraphs.text: The Jews therefore said, Behold how he loved him!
paragraphs.original: ἔλεγον οὖν οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι· Ἴδε πῶς ἐφίλει αὐτόν.
paragraphs.translit: elegon oun hoi Ioudaioi· Ide pōs ephilei auton.

paragraphs.text: But some of them said, Could not this man, who opened the eyes of him that was blind, have caused that this man also should not die?
paragraphs.original: τινὲς δὲ ἐξ αὐτῶν εἶπαν· Οὐκ ἐδύνατο οὗτος ὁ ἀνοίξας τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς τοῦ τυφλοῦ ποιῆσαι ἵνα καὶ οὗτος μὴ ἀποθάνῃ;
paragraphs.translit: tines de ex autōn eipan· Ouk edynato houtos ho anoixas tous ophthalmous tou typhlou poiēsai hina kai houtos mē apothanē;

paragraphs.text: Jesus therefore again groaning in himself cometh to the tomb. Now it was a cave, and a stone lay against it.
paragraphs.original: Ἰησοῦς οὖν πάλιν ἐμβριμώμενος ἐν ἑαυτῷ ἔρχεται εἰς τὸ μνημεῖον· ἦν δὲ σπήλαιον, καὶ λίθος ἐπέκειτο ἐπʼ αὐτῷ.
paragraphs.translit: Iēsous oun palin embrimōmenos en heautō erchetai eis to mnēmeion· ēn de spēlaion, kai lithos epekeito epʼ autō.

paragraphs.text: Jesus saith, Take ye away the stone. Martha, the sister of him that was dead, saith unto him, Lord, by this time the body decayeth; for he hath been [dead] four days.
paragraphs.original: λέγει ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Ἄρατε τὸν λίθον. λέγει αὐτῷ ἡ ἀδελφὴ τοῦ τετελευτηκότος Μάρθα· Κύριε, ἤδη ὄζει, τεταρταῖος γάρ ἐστιν.
paragraphs.translit: legei ho Iēsous· Arate ton lithon. legei autō hē adelphē tou teteleutēkotos Martha· Kyrie, ēdē ozei, tetartaios gar estin.

paragraphs.text: Jesus saith unto her, Said I not unto thee, that, if thou believedst, thou shouldest see the glory of God?
paragraphs.original: λέγει αὐτῇ ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Οὐκ εἶπόν σοι ὅτι ἐὰν πιστεύσῃς ὄψῃ τὴν δόξαν τοῦ θεοῦ;
paragraphs.translit: legei autē ho Iēsous· Ouk eipon soi hoti ean pisteusēs opsē tēn doxan tou theou;

paragraphs.text: So they took away the stone. And Jesus lifted up his eyes, and said, Father, I thank thee that thou heardest me.
paragraphs.original: ἦραν οὖν τὸν λίθον. ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς ἦρεν τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς ἄνω καὶ εἶπεν· Πάτερ, εὐχαριστῶ σοι ὅτι ἤκουσάς μου,
paragraphs.translit: ēran oun ton lithon. ho de Iēsous ēren tous ophthalmous anō kai eipen· Pater, eucharistō soi hoti ēkousas mou,

paragraphs.text: And I knew that thou hearest me always: but because of the multitude that standeth around I said it, that they may believe that thou didst send me.
paragraphs.original: ἐγὼ δὲ ᾔδειν ὅτι πάντοτέ μου ἀκούεις· ἀλλὰ διὰ τὸν ὄχλον τὸν περιεστῶτα εἶπον, ἵνα πιστεύσωσιν ὅτι σύ με ἀπέστειλας.
paragraphs.translit: egō de ēdein hoti pantote mou akoueis· alla dia ton ochlon ton periestōta eipon, hina pisteusōsin hoti sy me apesteilas.

paragraphs.text: And when he had thus spoken, he cried with a loud voice, Lazarus, come forth.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ταῦτα εἰπὼν φωνῇ μεγάλῃ ἐκραύγασεν· Λάζαρε, δεῦρο ἔξω.
paragraphs.translit: kai tauta eipōn phōnē megalē ekraugasen· Lazare, deuro exō.

paragraphs.text: He that was dead came forth, bound hand and foot with grave-clothes; and his face was bound about with a napkin. Jesus saith unto them, Loose him, and let him go.
paragraphs.original: ἐξῆλθεν ὁ τεθνηκὼς δεδεμένος τοὺς πόδας καὶ τὰς χεῖρας κειρίαις, καὶ ἡ ὄψις αὐτοῦ σουδαρίῳ περιεδέδετο. λέγει αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Λύσατε αὐτὸν καὶ ἄφετε αὐτὸν ὑπάγειν.
paragraphs.translit: exēlthen ho tethnēkōs dedemenos tous podas kai tas cheiras keiriais, kai hē opsis autou soudariō periededeto. legei autois ho Iēsous· Lysate auton kai aphete auton hypagein.

paragraphs.text: Many therefore of the Jews, who came to Mary and beheld that which he did, believed on him.
paragraphs.original: Πολλοὶ οὖν ἐκ τῶν Ἰουδαίων, οἱ ἐλθόντες πρὸς τὴν Μαριὰμ καὶ θεασάμενοι ἃ ἐποίησεν, ἐπίστευσαν εἰς αὐτόν·
paragraphs.translit: Polloi oun ek tōn Ioudaiōn, hoi elthontes pros tēn Mariam kai theasamenoi ha epoiēsen, episteusan eis auton·

paragraphs.text: But some of them went away to the Pharisees, and told them the things which Jesus had done.
paragraphs.original: τινὲς δὲ ἐξ αὐτῶν ἀπῆλθον πρὸς τοὺς Φαρισαίους καὶ εἶπαν αὐτοῖς ἃ ἐποίησεν Ἰησοῦς.
paragraphs.translit: tines de ex autōn apēlthon pros tous Pharisaious kai eipan autois ha epoiēsen Iēsous.

paragraphs.text: The chief priests therefore and the Pharisees gathered a council, and said, What do we? for this man doeth many signs.
paragraphs.original: συνήγαγον οὖν οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ Φαρισαῖοι συνέδριον, καὶ ἔλεγον· Τί ποιοῦμεν ὅτι οὗτος ὁ ἄνθρωπος πολλὰ ποιεῖ σημεῖα;
paragraphs.translit: synēgagon oun hoi archiereis kai hoi Pharisaioi synedrion, kai elegon· Ti poioumen hoti houtos ho anthrōpos polla poiei sēmeia;

paragraphs.text: If we let him thus alone, all men will believe on him: and the Romans will come and take away both our place and our nation.
paragraphs.original: ἐὰν ἀφῶμεν αὐτὸν οὕτως, πάντες πιστεύσουσιν εἰς αὐτόν, καὶ ἐλεύσονται οἱ Ῥωμαῖοι καὶ ἀροῦσιν ἡμῶν καὶ τὸν τόπον καὶ τὸ ἔθνος.
paragraphs.translit: ean aphōmen auton houtōs, pantes pisteusousin eis auton, kai eleusontai hoi Rhōmaioi kai arousin hēmōn kai ton topon kai to ethnos.

paragraphs.text: But a certain one of them, Caiaphas, being high priest that year, said unto them, Ye know nothing at all,
paragraphs.original: εἷς δέ τις ἐξ αὐτῶν Καϊάφας, ἀρχιερεὺς ὢν τοῦ ἐνιαυτοῦ ἐκείνου, εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Ὑμεῖς οὐκ οἴδατε οὐδέν,
paragraphs.translit: heis de tis ex autōn Kaiaphas, archiereus ōn tou eniautou ekeinou, eipen autois· Hymeis ouk oidate ouden,

paragraphs.text: nor do ye take account that it is expedient for you that one man should die for the people, and that the whole nation perish not.
paragraphs.original: οὐδὲ λογίζεσθε ὅτι συμφέρει ὑμῖν ἵνα εἷς ἄνθρωπος ἀποθάνῃ ὑπὲρ τοῦ λαοῦ καὶ μὴ ὅλον τὸ ἔθνος ἀπόληται.
paragraphs.translit: oude logizesthe hoti sympherei hymin hina heis anthrōpos apothanē hyper tou laou kai mē holon to ethnos apolētai.

paragraphs.text: Now this he said not of himself: but, being high priest that year, he prophesied that Jesus should die for the nation;
paragraphs.original: τοῦτο δὲ ἀφʼ ἑαυτοῦ οὐκ εἶπεν, ἀλλὰ ἀρχιερεὺς ὢν τοῦ ἐνιαυτοῦ ἐκείνου ἐπροφήτευσεν ὅτι ἔμελλεν Ἰησοῦς ἀποθνῄσκειν ὑπὲρ τοῦ ἔθνους,
paragraphs.translit: touto de aphʼ heautou ouk eipen, alla archiereus ōn tou eniautou ekeinou eprophēteusen hoti emellen Iēsous apothnēskein hyper tou ethnous,

paragraphs.text: and not for the nation only, but that he might also gather together into one the children of God that are scattered abroad.
paragraphs.original: καὶ οὐχ ὑπὲρ τοῦ ἔθνους μόνον, ἀλλʼ ἵνα καὶ τὰ τέκνα τοῦ θεοῦ τὰ διεσκορπισμένα συναγάγῃ εἰς ἕν.
paragraphs.translit: kai ouch hyper tou ethnous monon, allʼ hina kai ta tekna tou theou ta dieskorpismena synagagē eis hen.

paragraphs.text: So from that day forth they took counsel that they might put him to death.
paragraphs.original: ἀπʼ ἐκείνης οὖν τῆς ἡμέρας ἐβουλεύσαντο ἵνα ἀποκτείνωσιν αὐτόν.
paragraphs.translit: apʼ ekeinēs oun tēs hēmeras ebouleusanto hina apokteinōsin auton.

paragraphs.text: Jesus therefore walked no more openly among the Jews, but departed thence into the country near to the wilderness, into a city called Ephraim; and there he tarried with the disciples.
paragraphs.original: Ὁ οὖν Ἰησοῦς οὐκέτι παρρησίᾳ περιεπάτει ἐν τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις, ἀλλὰ ἀπῆλθεν ἐκεῖθεν εἰς τὴν χώραν ἐγγὺς τῆς ἐρήμου, εἰς Ἐφραὶμ λεγομένην πόλιν, κἀκεῖ ἔμεινεν μετὰ τῶν μαθητῶν.
paragraphs.translit: Ho oun Iēsous ouketi parrēsia periepatei en tois Ioudaiois, alla apēlthen ekeithen eis tēn chōran engys tēs erēmou, eis Ephraim legomenēn polin, kakei emeinen meta tōn mathētōn.

paragraphs.text: Now the passover of the Jews was at hand: and many went up to Jerusalem out of the country before the passover, to purify themselves.
paragraphs.original: Ἦν δὲ ἐγγὺς τὸ πάσχα τῶν Ἰουδαίων, καὶ ἀνέβησαν πολλοὶ εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα ἐκ τῆς χώρας πρὸ τοῦ πάσχα ἵνα ἁγνίσωσιν ἑαυτούς.
paragraphs.translit: Ēn de engys to pascha tōn Ioudaiōn, kai anebēsan polloi eis Hierosolyma ek tēs chōras pro tou pascha hina hagnisōsin heautous.

paragraphs.text: They sought therefore for Jesus, and spake one with another, as they stood in the temple, What think ye? That he will not come to the feast?
paragraphs.original: ἐζήτουν οὖν τὸν Ἰησοῦν καὶ ἔλεγον μετʼ ἀλλήλων ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ ἑστηκότες· Τί δοκεῖ ὑμῖν; ὅτι οὐ μὴ ἔλθῃ εἰς τὴν ἑορτήν;
paragraphs.translit: ezētoun oun ton Iēsoun kai elegon metʼ allēlōn en tō hierō hestēkotes· Ti dokei hymin; hoti ou mē elthē eis tēn heortēn;

paragraphs.text: Now the chief priests and the Pharisees had given commandment, that, if any man knew where he was, he should show it, that they might take him.
paragraphs.original: δεδώκεισαν δὲ οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ Φαρισαῖοι ἐντολὰς ἵνα ἐάν τις γνῷ ποῦ ἐστιν μηνύσῃ, ὅπως πιάσωσιν αὐτόν.
paragraphs.translit: dedōkeisan de hoi archiereis kai hoi Pharisaioi entolas hina ean tis gnō pou estin mēnysē, hopōs piasōsin auton.
